cultivation_relevance: Pearl Millet (Bajra) is a vital coarse cereal grown extensively in arid and semi-arid regions of India, particularly in Gujarat and Rajasthan. It serves as a staple food source providing high dietary energy, protein, and micronutrients, and acts as a crucial dual-purpose crop for grain and green fodder.

planting_details.sowing_time: July for Kharif season and February-March for Summer season
planting_details.spacing: 45 cm to 60 cm between rows and 10 cm to 15 cm between plants

nutrient_management.recommended_npk_ratio: N 32 kg, P 16 kg, K 0 kg per acre (varies by region)
micronutrients: Zinc Sulphate @ 8-10 kg per acre in zinc-deficient soils

harvest_and_yield.maturity_days: 70 to 90 days depending on the variety
harvesting_signs: Moisture content in grain drops below 20%
harvest_and_yield.expected_yield_per_acre: 8 to 12 quintals of grain, 15 to 20 quintals of dry fodder
harvest_and_yield.post_harvest_storage: Dry grains to 12% moisture level before storing in moisture-proof containers or hermetic bags.
